title: What is ICT?
description: Follow a message through input, processing, memory, storage and communication.

scenes.title: Three letters. One connected world.
scenes.narration: I C T means information and communication technology. It is the technology we use to work with information and share it. Let's follow a message.

scenes.title: First, give the computer input.
scenes.narration: You type hello on a keyboard. Those key presses are input: information entering the computer. A mouse, microphone, or touchscreen can provide input too.

scenes.title: The CPU follows instructions.
scenes.narration: The C P U runs the app's instructions. It processes your input so the letters appear on screen. Think of it as doing the work.

scenes.title: RAM is the working space.
scenes.narration: While the app is running, RAM holds data it is using right now. RAM is temporary. Turn the power off, and its contents are lost.

scenes.title: Storage keeps saved files.
scenes.narration: Save a file, and it goes to persistent storage, such as an S S D. Unlike RAM, saved files remain when the power is off.

scenes.title: Communication connects devices.
scenes.narration: Press send. A network carries your message as data between devices. On the other person's screen, the message becomes output: information they can see.

scenes.title: Put the pieces together.
scenes.narration: Input brings information in. The C P U processes it. RAM holds working data. Storage keeps saved files. Networks let devices share information. That's I C T.

scenes.title: Your turn: RAM or SSD?
scenes.narration: Quick check: which holds data a program is using right now? RAM. Next, open Task Manager and watch C P U, memory, disk, and network activity.
